title: psr-bilevel-eme-boundary: a reproduction of a public bi-level adiabatic polarization splitter-rotator (SOI 220 nm + 90 nm partial etch), and the boundary of a mode-expansion insertion loss: port basis, discretisation and solver defaults
description:
Scope -- carry this with any number you quote. A reproduction of the public BilevelPSR design on an SOI 220 nm + 90 nm partial-etch platform, verified in two independent segments by two different numerical methods: the taper segment by 3D FDTD (TM0 -> TE1 = 99.84%) and the coupler segment by 3D EME (TE1 -> lower-arm TE0 = 99.233%, passing a 4 -> 6 port-mode convergence check, delta = -0.29%).

The boundary is stated as a property of the numerical object, not of the device: a minimal S-bend, re-read on a second solver (EME, varFDTD and an exact bent-waveguide FDE solve, recorded in second_solver/), reads 0.055 / 0.765 / lossless for one nominal structure, and each numerical choice moves the reading once its feature is amplified.

Only those two port-mode-basis conversions may be quoted. Device-level absolute insertion loss and return loss are NOT certified here: in this structure the EME port-power column sums stay close to 1 even after adding port modes, so no radiation-loss channel appears inside the port-mode basis, and that figure would require an all-device 3D FDTD run or a measurement. The output section (S-bend plus the straight section, x = 405..537.8 um) was not covered. The falsification is scoped to this structure, this length scale and the 4 -> 6 mode comparison; it is not a general claim about eigenmode expansion.

Licence. Code (sim/, tools/, all *.py) is MIT; everything else (figures, data, documents, the notebook) is CC BY 4.0. That split is recorded in CITATION.cff and in the two LICENSE files. This record uses "Other (Open)" because Zenodo's licence field holds one identifier and cannot express the split.
